gen-shadows-into-light-fs-public-sans: Public Sans lays down a hefty, sturdy lowercase with broad openings in its c and s. Then Shadows Into Light scribbles over the top like casual pen marks, loosening up all that tidy weight.
gen-shadows-into-light-fs-supreme: Scrawled chalk-slate charm up top, over a dense, heavy strip of text that holds its letters open. Shadows Into Light is the casual voice; Supreme is the crisp sans.
gen-shadows-into-light-general-sans: General Sans reads smooth and clean, with a tall x-height filling each line. Shadows Into Light brings loose, wide-mouthed handwriting to the headline, while the sans keeps a steady pen pressure that carries the text.
gen-shadows-into-light-manrope: Manrope reads bright and approachable, with a generous gap at the mouth of every curve. Over a longer stretch, Manrope would feel like a marker line moving smoothly along, while Shadows Into Light keeps its crowded, chalky handwriting up top.
gen-shadows-into-light-satoshi: Satoshi reads tall and open, never squeezed. Shadows Into Light does casual, chalky handwriting best, crowding its letters like marks on a slate, while Satoshi keeps every stroke at one width, diagonals and uprights alike.
gen-shadows-into-light-switzer: Switzer reads wiry and tubular, with a tall waist line and tips that keep their distance. Shadows Into Light adds its crowded, wide-mouthed handwriting above, and the two feel like a hand-lettered note laid over a steady Swiss grid.
gen-shadows-into-light-work-sans: Work Sans comes across modern, with a high mean line and joins as sturdy as its strokes. And over many lines it would feel like ballpoint writing, while Shadows Into Light stays loose and friendly above it.
gen-comfortaa-lora: Lora reads bookish and warm, with a broad opening in its c. Comfortaa's neon-tube rings and stretched spacing sit above it, and the serif's sturdy hairlines keep a long page feeling literary rather than gimmicky.
gen-dafont-arkhip-lora: Lora reads literary, with modest thinning at its curves. Arkhip floats its widely spaced, uniform letters above, so the two feel like a geometric sign hung over a well-worn book.
gen-dafont-capture-it-fs-bespoke-slab: Urban and commanding, Capture It towers over the page with a sign-painter's single-stroke look. Its nearly sealed letters earn their keep big and short, while Bespoke Slab grounds things with tall, refined lowercase.
